messages:
Maya (PM): Heads-up from today's customer demo: our in-product docs panel and the public docs are using different naming in several spots. Users got confused between 'Pin model' vs 'Pin model version' and the deep links didn't land on the right section.

Kevin (Design): Saw that too. The panel's CTA is generic ('Learn more') and it jumps to the top of the page. We should deep-link and make the CTA explicit. Also the in-panel headings are Title Case while docs are sentence case. Tiny detail but noticeable.

Sylvia (DevEx): Current implementation calls docsService.link('models') which returns /docs/models. We can extend it to take an optional fragment or anchor id so components can request /docs/models#pin-model-version.

Raj (Eng): I can add support for anchor fragments and an optional ariaLabel param in the link helper. Will also include rel and target attributes when target=_blank is used. Any preference for whether these open in new tab?

Emma (A11y): External docs should open in a new tab and include rel="noopener noreferrer". Also add aria-label like 'Opens documentation in a new tab' and ensure keyboard users get the same affordance — the icon must be focusable and announceable.

Maya (PM): Decision: open docs in new tab for now (product team agreed), include aria-labels, and standardize copy to 'Pin model version' across console and docs. Docs team will add explicit heading id: '#pin-model-version'.

Kevin (Design): Can we change the CTA from 'Learn more' to 'See pinning docs'? Short and specific. Also recommend we standardize sentence case for in-panel headings to match the docs style guide.

Sylvia (DevEx): I'll add a small note to the docs style guide: 'Use sentence case for in-product snippets and anchor headings'. Also will add a redirect rule in case some external links rely on the old top-level URL.

Raj (Eng): I'll ship the link helper change and a unit test. ETA tomorrow AM. I will also ensure the generated anchor ids follow the pattern: kebab-case of the heading text.

Emma (A11y): Additional check: the in-panel close control needs aria-controls referencing the panel id. Can we adopt a predictable id convention like 'inlay-doc-<route>'?

Sylvia (DevEx): Yes: we'll use 'inlay-doc-models' for the models route. I'll include that mapping in the doc helper so components can pass the id when rendering.

DocBot: Note: Added a docs linter rule 'require-doc-anchors' that warns when a docs link without fragment is referenced from the console codebase. PR: https://git.internal/rdw/pulls/415

Kevin (Design): Another quick visual nit: the external link icon sits flush against the text in the small inlay. Add 4px spacing and ensure it scales at 16px on high-DPI.

Maya (PM): Action items condensed: (1) Raj: link helper changes + tests + open-in-new-tab behavior. (2) Sylvia: docs heading id for pinning, style guide note, redirect. (3) Kevin: update components and small spacing tweak; change CTA to 'See pinning docs'. (4) Emma: write the a11y checklist entries (aria-label, aria-controls, focusable icon/button).

Raj (Eng): Also adding a lightweight e2e that crawls console labels vs docs headings and surfaces mismatches in a report. Might save future triage.

Sylvia (DevEx): FYI I already found another mismatch: console uses 'Reserved capacity' in one attribute, docs use 'Dedicated capacity' elsewhere. I'll add it to the PR so we can pick a canonical term.

Maya (PM): Good catch. Let's default to 'Dedicated capacity' externally and show 'Reserved capacity' as legacy in parentheses where needed while we roll it out.

Kevin (Design): I'll update the mock to show the in-panel copy with the exact fragment link and spacings. Posting screenshots soon.

DocBot: Reminder: weekly docs sync Wednesday 10:00 AM.

Maya (PM): Thanks team. We'll reconvene here when PRs land and close the loop. :white_check_mark:
